page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz, with 24 physical cores and 2 threads per core. The processor includes 48 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes a bundled 1843 GB local SSD.

Benchmark data positions the D48ds_v5 as a balanced performer across diverse workloads. It achieves a Passmark CPU score of 48,717.7 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,064.0, both falling within the average tier. Memory performance is notable, with a Passmark memory score categorized as strong, supported by a read-only small block memory bandwidth of 2,502.0 GB/sec. Cryptographic capabilities are also strong, as demonstrated by a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 43,321.1. For language model tasks, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 275.95 tokens/sec on a small 135M model, though performance drops to a weak 2.74 tokens/sec for text generation on a large 70B model due to the lack of hardware GPU acceleration.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D48ds_v5 offers a balanced resource density, combining substantial compute capacity with a high-capacity local SSD without the premium cost of dedicated GPU hardware. This makes it a viable option for workloads requiring a mix of CPU power, memory, and fast local storage. Appropriate workloads include database operations, web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
